title:
The analytic container itself is an endpoint for Java-based action engine.

There are various dependencies between analytics, represented by the data in their input DFEs. The dependency types are:

 - metric: data should be available initially (possibly requiring aggregation)
 - transform: DFE is produced by an analytic
 - compound: DFE is assembled from multiple other DFEs
 - joined: DFE is assembled for multiple analytic results

When new data flows into the system, it is normalized and stored. For example, consumption,
temperature and meter event data. Each time the data loader finishes processing a block of input, it will trigger a
recalculation in the analytic container. This invalidation will list the metric and  date/time values.
This triggers re-evaluation of metric DFEs.

Other DFE types depend on analytics to produce them, so this re-evaluation fans out through the dependency tree,
queuing further analytics.

Some  configurations available to control analytic processing. These are available as TenantConfig.

###TenantConfig

 - ACE-StartOfTime : config to set the reference start time for period construction. value can be a date or a integer as number of days (+/-) from now.
```
 e.g. "2015-01-01", -200
```

- ACE-EndOfTime : config to set the reference end time for period construction. value can be a date or a integer as number of days (+/-) from now.
 ```
 e.g. "2018-01-01", -1
 ```

- ACE-MaxInvalDays : config to limit max number of days for period construction.
```
e.g: "365"
```


- ACE-AnalyticWhitelist : config to limit the analytics considered for execution. value is comma separated list of analytic names.
 ```
 e.g. "Analytic1, Analytic2"
 ```

- ACE-EnableMetricPriority : config to enable dynamic priorities in analytics/metrics queue invalidation {@link MetricPriority}

- ACE-AnalyticGroups : config to define the grouped analytic mapping as json value.
 ```
 e.g.
     {
       "ami": "AMIMeterHealthAP",
       "revpro": [ "RevenueOpportunityAP", "RevenueOpportunitySC" ],
       "other": "*"
     }
```
